how: The initiating member proposes the flag and coordinates, while subsequent joining is evidenced separately from that starter role.
Repeated invitations recruit members to start, enlarge and change the national flag.
Members give bare commitments to take on a fix or offer help.
Members request a sticky, moderators create a coordination venue and later proposals are redirected into it.
Members propose lettering, national landmarks and political additions, with some rejected for size and others left unanswered.
Members report the emerging flag, construction at a new location and completion of the rebuild.
Coordinates, templates and precise instructions align stripe widths, letter spacing and shared construction.
Automatic flag repair is shared and later challenged when its target conflicts with changed plans.
Maintenance follows completion and mistaken cleaning restores an outdated form, while eventual loss or abandonment from failed communication remains unestablished.
A reserved-space objection leads to a sharing request, permission and mutual protection terms.
Members discourage opening a neighbour's border and reject attacking a group that helped build their flag.
Visitors help construction, locals offer border security in return and another group's help request receives explicit acceptance.
A joint defence proposal, an alliance commitment and an official welcome establish coalition participation in the visible talk.
The banner request meets the revised entry's small-form permission-seeking range, while implementation and ongoing host rule remain provisional.
A visiting member explicitly calls themself a diplomat and apologises for damage, meeting the revised role's minimum range without proving binding authority.
A design-vote proposal and provisional agreement do not state binding-authority limits, while missing chats and replies prevent a whole-room negative.
A lettering prank repeatedly alters another national sign and recruits a member who reports doing their part.
National war joking and a report of resistance carry small canvas contests in talk.
Participants explain mistaken changes through ignorance of colour reversal and missed redesign instructions.
Historical wording in a prank call does not establish an actual intercommunity quarrel predating the canvas.
Calling the target colonials in the attack invitation supports same-turn historical framing without proving an established earlier community quarrel.
Participants explicitly judge their numbers insufficient and their contested position difficult to defend.
Relocation and rebuilding are explicitly connected to the earlier flag's erasure by an arriving helper.
Members celebrate making a name together and receive congratulations when the coordination sticky is removed.
Members mourn the ending, share a timelapse and guide viewers toward the finished area using a neighbouring flag.
Remembering an older flag and watching a recording supply no observed decision to continue the temporary canvas project elsewhere.
A viewer retracts an impression about imagery without correcting the room's history or contesting a preserved canvas version.
Apply the framing to proposing and policing a late hoax, because these concepts do not establish enacted fake news or a takeover.
National drinks, historical language and territorial analogies are carried into canvas encounters and political image proposals.
Speakers explicitly describe lightly used chat and their own coordination style as winging it and going with the flow.
Creating chat, posting invitations and directing painters there now fit the candidate's range, resolving the earlier missing-process objection while internal decisions remain unseen.
Disguising a colour change on the canvas does not establish private planning, coded communication or infiltration of rival venues.
An unanswered question asks how flag-making works, and a later viewer receives a landmark instruction locating the finished area.
A member of another national room comes to help and the offered help is welcomed, without establishing subscriber growth or durable membership.
Remembering a prior flag left at a company office does not show seeking company or press attention for the canvas work.
Treat the tactical move as preceding reported defeat, while prior encroachment prevents confirming the candidate's literal before-any-loss condition.
The big-wall reply and geographic-capture joke create humour from canvas borders and neighbouring flags.
Creating a chat for an existing national project does not by itself demonstrate a new canvas-born community forming around a pattern.
Reporting a proposed apartheid-flag overwrite identifies a threat without establishing a coded moral argument, refusal of hateful imagery or adjudication of an offensive joke.
Rejecting an attack on previous helpers as wrong supplies a narrow moral judgment about covering others' work rather than a general theory of conquest.
Dismissing pixel work does not demonstrate sabotage of the room's own mark or establish annoyance at subreddit posts as the motive of a reported overwrite.
A harsh correction and the target's explanation show interpersonal conflict around pixel work, while withdrawal, apology from the harsh speaker and reconciliation remain unestablished.
A question praising apparent overnight work suggests commitment but does not establish a participant's account of lost sleep, competing obligations or strain.
Keeping a tab open and enabling notifications do not establish site faults, timer exploits or fixes for them.
Visiting helpers and pixel-based unity do not establish dual community membership or conflicted loyalties.
Descriptions of winging it must remain compatible with a later proposed vote, without inferring either permanent informality or an implemented decision rule.
Automatic repair supports the selected design only while its target remains aligned with changed human plans.
Treat completion announcements as provisional occasions for praise that may be followed by correction and personal conflict.
The selected new spot is followed by reported construction, and a helper explicitly connects rebuilding to the prior erasure.
Received construction help supplies the explicit reason for refusing an attack on a neighbour.
Retain event-triggered recall of a prior mark, distinguishing an older object remembered through the canvas from work remade after it.
Retain the transition from a maker's flag story into ordinary employment questions as a supported local continuation outside the revised processes.
The call receives a construction proposal, but the cited text does not independently establish that recruitment caused actual placement.
Starting and calling coincide in one invitation, leaving a distinct earlier starter action causing a later call unobserved.
The rebuild's completion report explicitly identifies maintenance as the next task.
Upkeep and bargaining are visible, but the cited exchange does not establish maintaining an existing mark as the cause of border negotiation.
Restraint is justified by received help, leaving the settled-border mechanism unobserved despite borders and restraint both being present.
The script repairs blemishes, but its cited passage does not attribute automation to human upkeep being overwhelmed by attacks and the timer.
The completed flag becomes an explicit occasion to praise overnight work and its appearance.
Celebration precedes timelapse sharing, but no cited passage identifies celebrating as the reason the recording was posted.
Visible retrospective material supplies no decision to carry the temporary canvas project forward, leaving the recording-to-continuation mechanism unobserved.
The shortage speaker recommends diplomacy while another proposes moving, so the specific shortage-causes-relocation mechanism remains unresolved.
A lettering proposal receives a template, but the concepts do not establish that posting the template settled the design.
Bare commitments are visible, but separate top-level replies and a deleted intervening parent prevent testing the full preferred-answer mechanism in these examples.
Helpers assist unfinished construction without a cited local appeal establishing that maintenance shortages caused their recruitment.
Permission negotiations open into mutual protection and an explicit promise to provide assistance.
Recruitment precedes aggression, but the attack proponent names failed diplomacy rather than recruitment as the reason to attack.
A reply rejects attacking earlier helpers by explicitly judging that action wrong.
The cited speaker describes diplomacy failing before recommending attack, while no concept identifies that attack as causing a subsequent border agreement.
The lettering attack recruits an affirmative response and prompts its starter to report resistance to the prank.
Joint defence and alliance participation are observed, but the concepts do not establish local maintenance strain as the cause of coalition membership.
Canvas activity prompts demands for concentration, with a sticky request answered by moderator assent and a dedicated venue.
Bargaining and a proposed design vote do not demonstrate a stated commitment limit or authority dispute, while missing discussions prevent testing the bounded mechanism.
Members debate the value and location of pixel work through dismissals, an explanation of online unity and demands for a single thread.
